title: White Hermitage
subtitle: A white that ages for decades

steps.title: The hill
steps.body: Hermitage is a single granite hill above Tain-l'Hermitage, facing south. About a quarter of its wine is white, mostly Marsanne with some Roussanne. The granite and loess, with full southern sun, give rich, powerful whites. Chapoutier and Jean-Louis Chave are famous producers.

steps.title: A strange ageing curve
steps.body: White Hermitage is rich and fruity when young, then often closes up for several years, from about year 3 to 10, showing little aroma. After that, it opens again with honey, nuts, beeswax and dried fruit. The best can age 20 to 50 years, despite modest acidity, thanks to their concentration and phenolics.

steps.prompt: White Hermitage often goes through a closed, quiet phase before opening again with age.
steps.explanation: Yes. Many go quiet for several years, then develop honey and nutty complexity.

steps.title: Oak and style
steps.body: Producers make white Hermitage in different ways: some ferment and age in oak barrels for richness; others use old wood or steel to keep purity. Some sweet vin de paille, from dried grapes, is made in tiny amounts. Crozes-Hermitage whites are lighter and more affordable.
steps.highlight: Oaked or pure; sweet vin de paille

steps.prompt: Why can white Hermitage age for decades?
steps.explanation: Its acidity is modest; concentration and phenolic structure carry it.

steps.title: What you learned
points: White Hermitage is mostly Marsanne from a granite hill
It often closes up, then reopens with honey and nuts
